boardName: Taco’s Land style match — covers and food

styleContract.referenceRoles: Photographs control subjects and arrangement. Approved Taco’s Land assets control marks and technique. Initial style references were composited over pure white without changing artwork.
styleContract.coverScope: Only the two-tray sandwich cover and Jack eating outside the window include surroundings. Add descriptive detail without changing the ink-wash technique.
styleContract.foodScope: Food and complete serving trays or baskets only; no table, floor, grass, hand or other surrounding background.
styleContract.graziaPalette: Natural food colours. No blue pigment. The first blue paintings had the right technique, not the right palette.
styleContract.review: The user approved all six images after comparison in Paper. Integrated them into the local Grazia and Tacos Jaguar pages.

selectedArtwork.prompt: The FIRST reference photograph controls the actual scene, pose, proportions and object locations. The SECOND reference is the approved Taco’s Land lakeside ink-wash cover: it controls the EXACT mark-making, light pigment density, broken fine contours, translucent washes, small pooled ink accents and white open space. This is a new image in that same illustrated series, not a new style. Keep the same delicate wash technique and muted visual weight; add descriptive detail WITHIN that technique, not thick outlines or realistic rendering. Do not copy the lake scene or plates from the style reference. Cover scene with background: the short-haired man outside the cafe window bends down with a taco in his RIGHT hand and a dark paper cup in his LEFT hand. Preserve his actual face, sunglasses on top of his head, lowered eyes, nose, mouth, ear, bent neck, fingers and shirt folds. His face and hands need clear, small descriptive marks, not blank blobs. Retain the seated person's back of head and shoulder in the right foreground, the window structure, a hanging leafy plant on the left, the porch roof/eaves above, outdoor bushes and a few faint street and distant mountain marks seen THROUGH the window. Window lines are part of the real scene, not an added border. Break the outer edges into open strokes instead of a full rectangle. The man eating remains the focal point; background is lighter and less detailed. Same three pigments as the style reference: brick red #963d2e, dark brown #352b25, tan #d9c6aa. Create only one new illustration, not a collage. Plain solid pure white outside the artwork for later background removal; no off-white paper, paper grain, ground shadow, frame, caption or logos. Compose all intended marks within the central 70 percent of the canvas, with generous WHITE margins on EVERY side. Nothing cropped or touching an edge.

The SECOND reference is approved Taco’s Land painted artwork and controls the EXACT ILLUSTRATION STYLE. Make this look drawn by the same hand as the second image, part of the same small series. Match its broad flat opaque pigment shapes, chunky irregular dry brush edges, flat overlapping patches, strong open highlights and sparse dark accents. Use roughly the same brush size relative to the food. Do not draw every ingredient, bread pore or crease. No fine ink contours, watercolor shading, realistic texture, photorealism, gradients or detailed editorial food sketching. Food should read in a few bold hand-painted masses, just like the style reference. Do not copy the taco subject into a sandwich scene. Paint ONLY the two folded birria tacos, the round consomme cup at front left and their COMPLETE oval serving basket with its paper liner. Preserve this source photo's arrangement. Keep the complete outside basket silhouette: rim, sides and base edge. Use a few large simple lattice openings, not detailed wicker. Do not show just scattered fragments of a basket, and do not copy the round PLATE from the style reference. No table, placemat, napkin outside the basket or surroundings. Same palette as approved tacos: brick red #963d2e, dark brown #352b25 and tan #d9c6aa. Create only one new illustration, not a collage. Plain solid pure white outside the artwork for later background removal; no off-white paper, paper grain, ground shadow, frame, caption or logos. Compose all intended marks within the central 70 percent of the canvas, with generous WHITE margins on EVERY side. Nothing cropped or touching an edge.

intermediateRevisions.prompt: Refine the FIRST approved gouache illustration using the second photo as a reference for the container. Keep the exact existing painted food forms, colour palette and rough brushwork. The change is the basket: include the COMPLETE oval serving basket, all of its outside rim, sides and base edge, with the whole paper liner tucked into it. The basket must visibly support the tacos and cup, not a few disconnected arc fragments and not half a container. Retain the two folded birria tacos and the round consomme cup at the front left. Simplify the lattice to several deliberate chunky painted gaps, but do not erase structural parts of the basket. No table or placemat. Only brick red #963d2e, dark brown #352b25 and tan #d9c6aa. Pure solid white background for later removal, no paper grain or background tint. Entire basket and all food must fit inside central 70 percent of canvas. Complete clean silhouette and generous blank margins, no cropping.

Refine the FIRST approved gouache illustration using the second photograph for the whole serving container. Preserve the original loose opaque paint, irregular brushwork and food shapes: two open chicken tinga tacos with onion rings, crema and filling. Include the COMPLETE oval serving basket underneath, with all of its outside rim, sides and lower edge. The basket is a recognizable whole object, not partial floating rim fragments. Include a simplified complete paper liner tucked inside. Use a few chunky open lattice marks but keep all structural edges. Omit placemat, table and logo. Only brick red #963d2e, dark brown #352b25 and tan #d9c6aa. Pure solid white background for later removal, no paper grain or background tint. Entire basket and tacos occupy central 70 percent of canvas with blank margins on every side. No clipped objects.
